dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For fields q and production valued in a real normed vector space and a map flux, requires interval integrability of every spatial slice of q, every temporal slice of flux composed with q, every spatial slice of production, and every temporal function obtained by spatially integrating production. It also requires, for all real a,b,s,t, that the spatial integral of q at t minus that at s equal the time integral of flux(q(a,τ)) minus flux(q(b,τ)), plus the iterated production integral.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002

binders: Universally quantify q and production, each a function from a real spatial variable x and a real temporal variable t to E = (Fin 1 → Real). These are implicit Lean parameters but universal mathematical parameters.
Universally quantify speed=c over all real numbers. This single constant defines the flux map F:E→E by F(v)=c·v.
Assume h:LocalDef001(q,F,production). The five conclusions are conditional on this full hypothesis.
Every a,b,s,t in the integrability and integral-balance clauses ranges independently over all real numbers.

The existential statement binds a, then b, then s, then t within the equivalence for the fixed q,production,c. It requires one joint quadruple, with no requirement that its components be chosen independently of one another or of the fixed data.
In the derivative conclusion, a and b are universally quantified before the almost-everywhere quantification over t. The variable s in the differentiated function is a bound real time variable.
hypotheses: For every real a,b,t, x↦q(x,t) is μ-interval-integrable from a to b.
For every real x,s,t, τ↦c·q(x,τ) is μ-interval-integrable from s to t.
For every real a,b,t, x↦production(x,t) is μ-interval-integrable from a to b.
For every real a,b,s,t, τ↦P_ab(τ) is μ-interval-integrable from s to t.
For every real a,b,s,t, Q_ab(t)−Q_ab(s)=∫_s^t [c·q(a,τ)−c·q(b,τ)] dμ(τ)+R_ab(s,t).
conclusions: All five clauses of the assumed LocalDef001 package hold.
For every real a,b,s,t, R_ab(s,t)=(Q_ab(t)−Q_ab(s))−∫_s^t [c·q(a,τ)−c·q(b,τ)] dμ(τ).
The source-free integral balance property C(q,c) holds if and only if R_ab(s,t)=0_E for every real a,b,s,t.
The source-free integral balance property C(q,c) fails if and only if there exist real a,b,s,t such that R_ab(s,t)≠0_E.
For every real a,b, for μ-almost every real t, the ordinary derivative of s↦Q_ab(s) exists at t and equals c·q(a,t)−c·q(b,t)+P_ab(t).
mathematical_definitions: E is the real normed vector space of functions on the singleton set Fin 1={0}. Addition, subtraction, zero, and scalar multiplication are pointwise. Evaluating at 0 identifies E with the real line.
μ denotes the distinguished measure Real.measureSpace.volume. Its selection is fixed throughout the proposition; the packet does not expand the instance that chooses it.
Write ∫_a^b f dμ for the oriented vector integral ∫_(a,b] f dμ−∫_(b,a] f dμ. All integrals below are these interval integrals.
A function is μ-interval-integrable from a to b when it is integrable with respect to μ restricted to (a,b] and to (b,a].
Q_ab(u)=∫_a^b q(x,u) dμ(x) is the spatially integrated state at time u.
P_ab(u)=∫_a^b production(x,u) dμ(x) is the spatially integrated production at time u.
R_ab(s,t)=∫_s^t P_ab(τ) dμ(τ)=∫_s^t (∫_a^b production(x,τ) dμ(x)) dμ(τ), with space integrated first.

C(q,c) means: every spatial slice of q is interval-integrable on every real interval; for every x the temporal function τ↦c·q(x,τ) is interval-integrable on every real interval; and for all real a,b,s,t, Q_ab(t)−Q_ab(s)=∫_s^t [c·q(a,τ)−c·q(b,τ)] dμ(τ).
Having derivative v at t means that the difference quotient of Q_ab at t converges to v in E as the nonzero real increment tends to zero.
A property holds μ-almost everywhere when its failure set has μ-outer measure zero.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For any one-coordinate real state field q, one-coordinate real production field, and constant real speed c, assume all the specified spatial and temporal interval-integrability conditions and the integral balance law with flux v↦c·v and production. Then that entire balance package holds; the iterated production integral on every oriented space-time rectangle equals the change in spatially integrated state minus the time-integrated left-minus-right boundary flux; the source-free integral balance package holds exactly when every such production integral is zero; it fails exactly when some such integral is nonzero; and, for each fixed spatial interval, the spatially integrated state has ordinary time derivative equal to its left-minus-right boundary flux plus spatially integrated production at almost every time with respect to the specified measure.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The state dimension is exactly one. The generic normed-space binders in the local definitions do not make the target a theorem for arbitrary state dimension or arbitrary normed spaces.
The flux is restricted to multiplication by one fixed real constant c. There is no arbitrary nonlinear flux or space-dependent or time-dependent speed.
No assumption requires c to be positive or nonzero. At c=0, temporal integrability of c·q(x,τ) places no temporal integrability requirement on q(x,τ) itself.
All space and time variables range over the entire real line. There are no initial conditions, boundary conditions, finite physical domain, or nonnegative-time restriction.
No endpoint inequalities are imposed. Integrals are oriented, and rectangles with a=b or s=t have zero iterated integral, so they cannot witness the nonzero existential conclusion.
The derivative's exceptional null set may depend on a and b. The target does not assert one common set of full measure on which the formula holds for all spatial intervals.

The assumption already includes the complete integral balance identity. The first conclusion repeats the assumption, and the rearranged identity and equivalences are conditional consequences of that strong package.

The integrability clauses prevent the displayed identities from relying merely on default values of nonintegrable integrals. They require all spatial slices listed, each temporal flux slice, and each time-dependent spatial production integral to be interval-integrable.
The statement uses an iterated integral with space first. It does not separately assume joint integrability of production on product rectangles or assert an exchange of integration order.
No positivity of q or production is required. A nonzero production integral can have either sign in its single coordinate.
The zero-integral characterization is stated in terms of all iterated production integrals. It does not explicitly assert pointwise or almost-everywhere vanishing of production.

The conclusion differentiates the spatial integral of q. It does not explicitly assert spatial or temporal pointwise differentiability of q, or the pointwise partial differential equation ∂_t q+c·∂_x q=production.
The target does not assert existence or uniqueness of fields satisfying the assumed package.

All almost-everywhere and integral statements depend on the selected real measure. A degenerate measure could make such assertions vacuous; the supplied inferInstance body does not itself expose a nondegeneracy or normalization certificate.
ambiguities: D073 exposes Real.measureSpace only as inferInstance. The packet therefore does not independently identify its distinguished measure or establish its normalization. The translation is exact using μ=Real.measureSpace.volume; interpreting every dμ as ordinary Lebesgue dx or dt requires the missing instance expansion.
